item.title: Patriots’ Maye turns ball over 3 times while hounded by Seahawks’ defense in Super Bowl loss
item.description: Drake Maye was a dependable and steadying force for the New England Patriots this season. The second-year quarterback never got the chance to be that when his team needed him most in the Super Bowl. Maye was the NFL’s most accurate passer during the regular season and finished second in MVP voting. But he was hounded by the Seahawks' pass rush throughout. item.title: Yes, there was a real wedding during Bad Bunny’s Super Bowl halftime show
item.description: Bad Bunny's Super Bowl halftime show featured a real wedding. About five minutes into the performance at Levi's Stadium, a couple was married on stage. item.description: Kenneth Walker III is running into free agency with a Super Bowl MVP. item.title: Puerto Rico stops for 13 minutes to applaud history and bask in Bad Bunny’s glow
item.description: For many Puerto Ricans in San Juan and beyond, the Super Bowl lasted all of 13 minutes. item.title: New Zealand mosque shooter seeks to discard his guilty pleas, saying prison made him irrational
item.description: Brenton Tarrant, who killed 51 Muslim worshipers in New Zealand’s deadliest mass shooting, is asking an appeals court to discard his guilty pleas. He says he was forced to admit to the crimes due to harsh prison conditions affecting his mental state. A panel of three judges at the Court of Appeal in Wellington is hearing evidence starting Monday about his fitness to plead to the charges. item.title: Tokyo’s benchmark Nikkei 225 jumps after a landslide victory for PM Takaichi’s ruling party
item.description: Asian shares have advanced and Tokyo's Nikkei 225 share index jumped as much as 5% after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s governing party secured a two-thirds supermajority in a parliamentary election. The landslide victory gives Takaichi a stronger mandate to pursue market-friendly policies. item.description: Seattle Seahawks star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba returned in the fourth quarter of Super Bowl 60 after being taken to the locker room in the third quarter to be evaluated for a concussion.
